findings.title: ShinyHunters: Cyber Criminal Group Attacks Learning Management System
findings.summary_md: FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center PSA I-051526-PSA warning about ShinyHunters attacks on a learning management platform. The advisory states the group uses real or exaggerated claims of data access to extort victims, harasses victims and relatives with threatening calls and texts, uses swatting, and often falsely claims to hold compromising material. This is the public warning ShinyHunters demands the bureau retract.

findings.title: ShinyHunters Targets Education Sector with Oracle PeopleSoft Exploit
findings.summary_md: Mandiant and Google Threat Intelligence Group attribute a May 27 to June 9, 2026 extortion campaign to ShinyHunters (UNC6240) exploiting CVE-2026-35273, a CVSS 9.8 RCE in PeopleSoft Environment Management, ahead of Oracle's June 10 advisory. Over 100 organizations were notified, 68 percent in higher education, with stolen data posted to the ShinyHunters leak site on June 9. The post documents MeshCentral C2 at wss://azurenetfiles.net:443/agent.ashx, staging hosts 142.11.200.186 through 190, and hunting guidance for /PSEMHUB/hub exploitation traffic.

findings.title: 'We Hacked the FBI:' Hackers Say They Have Data on All FBI Employees
findings.summary_md: Joseph Cox's first report on the breach claim, quoting a ShinyHunters representative: 'We hacked the FBI. We hold data on all FBI employees and applicants.' 404 Media reviewed a sample of 5,000 alleged records containing names, addresses, phone numbers, and spouse details. The article frames the exposure as a counterintelligence and harassment risk, noting criminals have previously used stolen data to track and intimidate FBI agents investigating them.

findings.title: ShinyHunters claims FBI hack, data theft in PeopleSoft zero-day breach
findings.summary_md: Lawrence Abrams details the group's claims: a new unpatched Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day RCE used Monday night, lateral movement into FBI-managed AWS GovCloud, and 2 to 3 TB of employee and applicant data, with apply.fbijobs.gov defaced. The FBI confirmed it is investigating unauthorized activity affecting FBIjobs.gov without confirming a breach. ShinyHunters tied the attack to its demand that the FBI retract the May 2026 FLASH report within one week and said it denies the swatting and false-claims allegations in that advisory.
